p: faint by the way: Literally, "they will fall apart", or "be dissolved", for when men faint they tear their muscles.
And the Pharisees: The stubborn enemies of the doctrine of the Gospel, giving no credit to the miracles already done, require new ones: but Christ, being angry with them, utterly forsakes them.
came forth: A common saying which the Hebrews use, by which is meant that the Pharisees went from their houses to purposely engage him.
sighed deeply in his spirit: These sighs came from the centre of his heart for the Lord was very much moved with the great unbelief of these men.

There shall no sign be given: Literally, "If a sign be given". It is an abbreviated kind of speech very common among the Hebrews; it is the same as when we say, "Let me be taken for a liar", or something similar. And when they speak out the whole, they say, "The Lord do such and such by me."
And he charged them: We must especially take heed of those who corrupt the word of God, no matter what their position is in the Church or in civil politics.
And they reasoned among themselves: They that have their minds fixed on earthly things are utterly blinded to heavenly things, even though they are plainly set before them.
How is it that ye do: How does it come to pass that you do not understand these things which are so plain and evident.
And he cometh to Bethsaida: A true image of our regeneration, which Christ, separating us from the world, works and accomplishes in us gradually.
see men as trees: He perceived men moving but at the same time could not discern their bodies.
look up: He commanded him to try again, to determine whether or not he could indeed see well.
And he sent him away to: Christ will not have his miracles to be separated from his doctrine.
And Jesus went out: Many praise Christ, who yet nonetheless rob him of his praise.

And he charged them that they: Christ has appointed certain times for the preaching of the gospel, and therefore here defers it to a more appropriate time, lest sudden haste should rather hinder than further the mystery of his coming.
And he began to teach them: All that Christ suffered for us he suffered not unwillingly, neither as being unaware, but foreknowing it and willingly.
And he spake that saying openly: None are more mad than they that are wise without the word of God.
savourest not the things that be: This is not godly, but worldly wisdom.
And when he had called the: The disciples of Christ must bear bravely whatever burden the Lord lays upon them, and subdue the desires of the flesh.
For what shall it profit a: They are the most foolish of all men who purchase the pleasures of this life with the loss of everlasting bliss.
